description: Hi, I’m Anurag Sagar. I’m building a team for the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective" challenge to analyze NASA Earth data & build an interactive trend dashboard.
summary:
We developed Earth System Trend Detective, an interactive, AI-assisted climate intelligence web platform that turns raw NASA Earth observation data into clear, scientifically validated insights.
​To address the challenge of navigating vast satellite datasets and identifying meaningful environmental changes, our tool features a guided "Data Detective" Wizard that recommends relevant NASA variables (such as MODIS temperature/vegetation, GPM rainfall, and GLDAS soil moisture) with plain-English definitions. Users can select single locations or compare two contrasting regions side-by-side to uncover how a single planetary driver causes opposite trends in different areas. Our Python-based statistical and machine learning pipeline automatically strips away recurring seasonal cycles (de-seasoning), detects historical anomalies, forecasts future trajectories, and runs Mann-Kendall and linear regression significance tests to prove whether a shift is statistically significant (p < 0.05) or merely natural fluctuation.
​This project is important because it democratizes complex climate science for students, educators, and citizen scientists. By bridging the gap between raw satellite data and rigorous statistical validation, it empowers everyday users to independently investigate what is changing, where, and how fast—fostering data-driven climate literacy.
details:
Project Overview: Earth System Trend Detective (Project YELLOWJACKET):

​1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work? ​Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive, AI-assisted climate intelligence platform designed to help students, researchers, and citizen scientists uncover, analyze, and validate long-term environmental trends using authentic NASA Earth observation datasets. ​How It Works (The 4-Step Pipeline): ​Guided Variable Discovery ("Data Detective" Wizard): Instead of overwhelming users with hundreds of complex satellite parameters, the platform asks a short series of intuitive questions (e.g., Target biome, environmental concern, or region). An AI matching engine maps their answers to relevant NASA variables (like Land Surface Temperature, Soil Moisture, or NDVI) along with plain-English definitions. ​Automated Data Acquisition & De-trending: Once a user selects a region (or two contrasting regions) on the interactive map, the backend pulls multi-decade monthly time-series data from NASA datasets. Our ML pipeline automatically strips away recurring seasonal noise (de-seasoning) so underlying long-term shifts become clearly visible. ​Statistical Significance & Forecasting Engine: The system calculates the exact rate of change (linear slope) and runs rigorous scientific validation—including the Mann-Kendall Trend Test, p-value calculations, and Confidence Intervals—to prove whether a shift is statistically significant or just natural fluctuation. Machine learning models (Prophet/ARIMA and Isolation Forest) also detect historical climate anomalies and forecast 5-to-10-year trajectories. ​Dual-Region Side-by-Side Visualization: Users can compare two geographically distinct regions simultaneously to observe how a single global climate driver causes opposite trends in different places (e.g., severe drought in one region paired with extreme precipitation in another). ​2. What Benefits Does It Have? ​Eliminates Data Paralysis: Bridges the gap between raw, complex NASA satellite data formats (NetCDF/HDF5) and actionable human understanding through guided variable recommendations and jargon-free definitions. ​Scientific Rigor Made Accessible: Automates complex statistical testing (p-values, Mann-Kendall Tau, seasonal decomposition) with a single click, turning raw graphs into scientifically defensible conclusions. ​Reveals Hidden Patterns: By separating seasonal cycles from long-term trends and flagging sudden anomalies, users can spot subtle environmental shifts that standard raw line charts hide. ​Built-in Learning Mode: Features pre-loaded interactive case studies (e.g., Deforestation vs. Regional Surface Temperature) so beginners can immediately learn how Earth system variables interact. ​3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project? ​Democratizing Earth Science: Empowers high school students, university researchers, educators, and policymakers to conduct genuine, publication-grade trend analysis without needing advanced coding or remote-sensing expertise. ​Promoting Systems Thinking: By highlighting dual-region opposite trends, the tool helps the public understand that Earth is a deeply interconnected system—local environmental changes are often tied to broader planetary processes. ​Data-Driven Climate Literacy: Combats climate misinformation by giving everyday users a transparent tool to verify for themselves what is changing, where, how fast, and whether the evidence is statistically significant. ​4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used ​NASA Data Sources & Models: ​NASA POWER & Giovanni APIs ​Satellite Instruments: MODIS (Vegetation Index/NDVI & Land Surface Temperature), GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) ​Global Assimilation Models: GLDAS (Soil Moisture & Evaporation) & MERRA-2 (Atmospheric Variables) ​Programming Languages: Python (Backend, Data Engineering, AI/ML), JavaScript / TypeScript (Frontend UI). ​AI, Machine Learning & Statistics Stack: ​Scikit-Learn (Isolation Forest for anomaly detection, clustering) ​Prophet & Statsmodels (Time-series forecasting & seasonal decomposition) ​SciPy & pyMannKendall (Mann-Kendall trend tests, linear regression slopes, p-value & confidence interval validation) ​Pandas, NumPy, Xarray, & GeoPandas (Multi-dimensional NetCDF/CSV wrangling and spatial aggregation) ​Backend & API Architecture: FastAPI / Flask (RESTful APIs serving raw, de-trended, and statistical JSON payloads). ​Frontend & Visualization Stack: React.js / Next.js, TailwindCSS, Mapbox GL / Leaflet (Interactive geospatial selection), and Plotly / Chart.js (Side-by-side interactive time-series and confidence interval graphs). ​Development, Collaboration & Hardware: VS Code, Jupyter Notebooks, Git & GitHub (Branch-based CI/CD workflow), Cloud Hosting (Vercel/Render), developed across standard multi-core laptops. ​5. How Is Your Project Creative? ​The "Data Detective" Paradigm: Rather than building another passive map dashboard, we gamified and structured the user journey around investigative storytelling—guiding users from curiosity to hypothesis testing, and finally awarding an instant "Significance Scorecard" badge to their findings. ​Dual-Region "Opposite Trend" Explorer: Most climate tools look at one location in isolation. Our split-screen spatial comparator is uniquely engineered to demonstrate teleconnections—showing how one atmospheric or oceanic driver pushes a variable up in Region A while pulling it down in Region B. ​Raw vs. De-Trended Toggle: Giving users a live switch to peel away seasonal weather cycles (summer/winter spikes) and watch the true multi-decade climate signal emerge makes complex statistical concepts visually intuitive. ​6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider? ​Target Audience Accessibility: Because the primary audience includes students and science-curious citizens, we prioritized plain-English variable definitions, intuitive UI workflows, and pre-built demonstration examples over dense academic interfaces. ​Signal vs. Noise (Statistical Integrity): Earth data is notoriously noisy due to seasonal cycles. We specifically factored in seasonal decomposition and explicitly distinguished between "Trending & Significant (p < 0.05)" versus "Emerging Trend (Needs Longer Data)" so users never misinterpret short-term weather fluctuations as long-term climate trends. ​Temporal & Spatial Resolution: While NASA offers hourly data, processing multi-decade hourly datasets causes severe latency. We optimized our pipeline around monthly and daily temporal resolutions and pre-aggregated spatial coordinates to ensure fast, responsive browser performance. ​Scalable System Architecture: Our team structured the project into decoupled microservices (Data Pipeline, Statistical/ML Engine, REST API, and Interactive UI) so new NASA datasets and regions can be plugged in seamlessly without rewriting the frontend.
